items.textToSpeech: For adults aged 19+, including those pregnant or lactating, the Upper Level of Intake for vitamin A is 3,000 micrograms per day, in the form of retinol. Although β-carotene is a precursor of vitamin A, excess intake has not been associated with vitamin A toxicity in humans, as the metabolic conversion of β-carotene is regulated by vitamin A status. An Upper Level of Intake for β-carotene from food does not need to be established, based on an absence of adverse effects.

There is insufficient evidence to establish an Upper Level of Intake for β-carotene for supplemental use, but high intakes can cause yellowing of the skin and may be harmful to smokers. The Upper Level is the highest average daily nutrient intake level likely to pose no adverse health effects to almost all individuals in the general population. For Australia and New Zealand, Nutrient Reference Values are published by the National Health and Medical Research Council. Is there anything else I can help you with?
